endorsements.quote: The development stage requires detailed documentation of model origins, intended use, and ethical considerations.
Like Abu Dhabi, Dubai mandates independent third-party validation of AI systems for objective veri fication.
For example, researchers should establish their compliance with Qatar’s data protection law (Law No. 13 of 2016) alongside global frameworks such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)31.

unlisted_practices: Embed healthcare law and ethics principles such as informed consent, liability, and patient rights across all phases of the AI lifecycle: research and development, approval, and post-implementation.
Establish a certification process for researchers who comply with healthcare AI development guidelines.
Provide built-in mechanisms for end-users to appeal AI system decisions.
Require graceful degradation mechanisms so AI systems fail safely in high-stakes environments.
Adapt AI development guidelines to the local context and target population, including documenting how systems accommodate patients who are not fluent in the local languages.

screen.reason: This paper presents a conceptual governance framework ('True Lifecycle Approach') for healthcare AI across development, deployment, and use, focusing on legal and ethical principles.
